title: Direct-send relay refusal and bypass use the physical queue front while relay authority uses the runnable position, so a refused relay behind a historical row is promoted and the user prompt stalls
outcome: Relay refusal ownership, the ordinary-user bypass and the FIFO decisions in direct send all use the same runnable-queue selector (ordinary_queue_position) as relay authority validation. A refused relay carrier that sits behind a non-runnable historical row is held, not promoted, and a fresh user prompt runs.
acceptance: A behavioural test: an idle, unpaused queue [non-runnable historical non-relay row, runnable relay carrier whose enrollment is revoked or whose metadata is missing]. A fresh user prompt runs as the next turn; the refused relay carrier is NOT promoted; both prior rows remain unchanged
Refusal capture and the bypass predicates select the same queue entry as validate_front_mailbox_relay_authority (ordinary_queue_position), with no remaining physical-front assumption on these paths
